text:
anika: Quick share — ran a microprofile across TP all-reduce for the 16k-token workload and I'm seeing a surprising idle gap during backward where GPUs wait on NCCL all-reduce for ~1.8ms per step.
raj: Can you paste the profiling snippet and nccl version? param sizes?
anika: nvprof snippet + nccl version below. I'm on nccl 2.17.4, CUDA 11.8
```
# summary from perf script
step 345: forward 6.2ms | attn-kernel 2.1ms | matmul 1.8ms | backward all-reduce wait 1.8ms | compute overlap 0.3ms
nccl ops: allreduce bytes=1.6MB count=20000 dtype=float16
``` 
raj: That bytes number is interesting — 1.6MB per all-reduce puts us in the regime where ring vs tree tradeoffs flip. ring latency scales with n*alpha + msg*(beta) while tree better for mid-sized with fewer hops.
tyler: Are these contiguous large tensors or many small tensors? NCCL performance can tank if we have many tiny ops (kernel launch overhead) vs aggregated large op.
anika: It's a single contiguous KV-based tensor per shard, but the serving runtime slices it into ~8 segments to match our batching heuristic (we split by attention head groups). So we end up issuing 8 all-reduces per step.
emma: Splitting helps compute parallelism but multiplies comm heads. 8*1.6MB=> 12.8MB total moved but with repeated startup costs. Try coalescing before calling nccl.
perf-bot: perf/regression detected: TP_allreduce_tailgap increased by 22% vs baseline (2024-11-02). Triggering investigation.
raj: Two quick experiments: (1) switch NCCL_COLL_TREE (if supported) or set NCCL_ALGO=tree; (2) coalesce segments into fewer larger all-reduces and measure.
tyler: Also measure comm/compute overlap by stalling compute artificially (cudaEvent timings). If overlap is poor it's likely scheduling or cudaStream ordering.
anika: Ran both: setting NCCL_ALGO=tree reduced per-op latency from 1.8ms -> 1.1ms but total end-to-end didn't fully recover because we still had 8 ops. Coalescing to 2 ops (4 segments each) cut total all-reduce time by 48% and GPU occupancy improved.
```
# coalesced run
step 412: forward 6.0ms | attn-kernel 2.0ms | matmul 1.7ms | all-reduce total 2.1ms | overlap 1.1ms
```
emma: Good. But watch out for memory peak — coalescing increases temporary buffer and KV cache alignment can cause extra copies.
anika: Noted. I also observed that KV cache hit pattern matters: repeated short queries cause small effective batch sizes, which degenerates to many tiny all-reduces because we slice per-request sequence length. So workload shape matters a lot.
raj: Could we adapt batching heuristic: if avg seq_len < threshold, use fewer partitions to avoid many small comms? Or switch to reduce-scatter + allgather pattern which is more bandwidth-friendly for large tensor across many ranks.
tyler: reduce-scatter + allgather also allows better overlap if you pipeline chunks; but it requires codepath changes in our runtime. Might be worth for Dedicated customers.
anika: Also tested message size sweep using nccl-tests: for N ranks=8, latency curve has inflection around 512KB-2MB. Below 512KB ring wins, above ~2MB tree starts to be beneficial depending on topology. Our 1.6MB per segment sits right in the messy middle.
emma: For immediate mitigation: 1) set default NCCL_ALGO=tree for TP jobs, 2) runtime coalesce threshold tuned to avoid <512KB per segment, 3) add a telemetry metric for per-op msg size histogram.
perf-bot: action created: PERF-3167 "TP allreduce msgsize histogram + coalesce tuning" assigned to anika. SLA 2w
anika: I'll prototype a coalesce-first path and run full regression harness across 4/8/16 GPUs and post numbers.
raj: Also add a test case where KV cache returns variable seq_len distribution (bursting small/large) — we should ensure heuristics don't oscillate.
tyler: FYI: NVSHMEM could give lower peer-to-peer lat for mid sized messages on DGX; maybe try NVSHMEM transport as optional in Dedicated builds.
anika: Good point, will spike. If anyone wants the raw perf traces I uploaded them to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/2024-11/tp-allreduce/msgsize-sweep-1718023345
emma: Nice work. Short-term mitigation + telemetry + perf ticket is a solid plan. :thumbsup:
anika: Thanks — will update thread with numbers and PR link.
